newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean defector shot, injured near Seoul.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector shot, injured near Seoul.

text.p: A North Korean defector to South Korea has been shot and injured by two gunmen in an attack near Seoul apparently ordered by the communist state, a senior police officer told Reuters.

The police officer said he suspected the gunmen were North Korean agents ordered to send a stark warning to the South following the defection of a high North Korean official, now holed up in the South Korean mission in Beijing.

The officer, who asked not to be named, identified the injured man as Li Il-nam (known in South Korea as Lee Han-yong), and described him as the nephew of a girlfriend of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.

Li, 36, was shot outside his home at Bundang, just south of Seoul, late on Saturday, the police officer said. A nurse at a nearby hospital said the defector later underwent surgery but she gave no details of his condition.
Tensions on the divided peninsula have flared since Wednesday, when Hwang Jang-yop, a member of the secretariat of North Korea's ruling Workers' Party, arrived by taxi at Seoul's Beijing mission.

South Korea says Hwang is seeking asylum in the South, while a furious North Korea insists he was kidnapped. Hwang was ranked 24th in the Stalinist state's hierarchy, and would be the most senior Pyongyang official to seek asylum in the South.

The Chinese government must now decide on Hwang's future -- whether to allow him to be flown to Seoul, where he could be expected to reveal crucial secrets about the North Korean state, or to send him back to Pyongyang. Hwang's apparent betrayal has caused a massive loss of face for a North Korean government already reeling from severe food shortages and economic disasters. Fearing retaliation, Seoul has ordered tighter security at all its overseas missions.

The South Korean police officer said, meanwhile, that a full-scale manhunt was under way for the presumed North Korean gunmen. Li is the first North Korean defector to be shot in South Korea since the end of the 1950-53 Korean War, the officer added.
Despite the 1953 truce, the two Koreas have remained implacable foes and their tense common border, bristling with advanced weapons, is today the last Cold War frontier.
